title: Reliability Pulsecard + Oncall Escalation Handoff
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight, machine-readable Pulsecard artifact and oncall handoff process that binds SLIs, SLOs, error budget state, and escalation actions to each reliability initiative. The Pulsecard should be consumable by the Console dashboard and by oncall automation for fast remedial decisions.
background: Teams at Redwood maintain SLIs & SLOs in disparate dashboards. During incidents it's time-consuming for oncall to determine active initiatives, remaining error budget, and pre-authorized remedial actions. This ticket standardizes a Pulsecard schema and rollout plan to reduce mean time to decision and to automate escalation when error budgets cross thresholds.
goals: 1) Define Pulsecard schema and minimal fields for runbooks and automation. 2) Implement server-side transformation that emits Pulsecards for each initiative. 3) Integrate Pulsecards into Console initiative view and oncall Slack+PagerDuty flows. 4) Validate with a pilot that oncall decision time drops by 30%.
success_metrics:
- Pulsecard generation coverage: 80% of active reliability initiatives by end of sprint
- Oncall median time-to-decision reduced by 30% in pilot
- Automated escalations triggered correctly >=95% in simulated runs
- Adoption: 3 teams onboarded to use the Pulsecard in runbooks
deliverables:
- Pulsecard schema doc (JSON schema)
- Migration guide for Product/Engineering
- Console UI card to show current SLI, SLO, error budget burn, and authorized rollback actions
- Automation hook (webhook + signed token) for PagerDuty/Slack to trigger pre-approved mitigations
- Pilot run with Observability and Runtime teams
acceptance_criteria:
- Schema is reviewed and accepted by Runtime, Observability, and Security
- Console shows Pulsecard for pilot initiatives with live SLI/SLO values
- Oncall automation uses Pulsecard to generate a clear incident checklist when burn>50%
- Post-pilot retrospective with actionable items
milestones: 2025-02-18: Draft Pulsecard schema and runbook field list
2025-03-05: Console prototype card integrated with mock Pulsecards
2025-03-18: Pilot run with two initiatives and oncall playthrough
risks: Schema creep: teams try to add many optional fields, increasing integration cost
Data drift: SLI queries diverge between dashboards and Pulsecard snapshots
Automation hazard: incorrectly authorized mitigations could affect customer traffic
Dependence on Console API changes from Observability team
decisions: Keep Pulsecard minimal: five required fields (initiative_key, sli_id, slo_target, error_budget_pct, authorized_actions)
Use signed webhook tokens for automation instead of full service account credentials
Pilot integration will be read-only for first run (no automatic rollbacks), automation will generate suggested actions in Slack
notes: Referenced existing SLO artifacts: console:/dashboards/reliability-overview and drive:/SLO-inventory-2025.xlsx
Talked with Observability about adding a /pulsecard endpoint to the metrics service
Runtime team prefers a compact schema to avoid extra KV lookups during high QPS
